news.title: English FA calls for Infantino to release World Cup sell-off documents
news.lede: The chair of the English Football Association has called on FIFA president Gianni Infantino to release all the documentation relating to the abandoned plan to sell a stake in the World Cup to private investors. Infantino's proposal was short-lived after a fierce backlash from across the sport, with European governing body UEFA threatening to boycott all FIFA competitions until it was shelved. FA chair Debbie Hewitt, who is also a FIFA vice-president and a member of the FIFA Council, has written to Infantino asking for full disclosure of all information relating to the scheme before the FIFA Council next meets on October 15. Hewitt has also called for the release of documents relating to the decision to suspend a ban handed to United States striker Folarin Balogun during the World Cup, which followed a phone call from US President Donald Trump to Infantino.

news.title: Azerbaijan simplifies visa procedures for FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival
news.lede: Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev has signed an order simplifying visa procedures for foreigners and stateless persons travelling to Azerbaijan for the inaugural FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival. As reported by İdman.Biz, citing AZERTAC, eligible visitors arriving in connection with the tournament will be able to obtain visas at Azerbaijan's international airports from September 22 to November 5, 2026. To qualify for the simplified procedure, visitors must present one of the documents specified in the presidential order. These include an official invitation letter from the Association of Football Federations of Azerbaijan (AFFA) or a document confirming accreditation through FIFA's electronic registration system in accordance with the governing body's relevant regulations.

news.title: Hungarian Education Minister Draws Ire of Football Fans with Ignorant Comments
news.lede: Comments Minister of Education Judit Lannert of Hungary made shortly after Hungary's loss to Ireland in the FIFA World Cup qualifiers have angered fans of multiple Hungarian football clubs. In the unearthed statements, Lannert spoke disparagingly about fans who cried after the national team's loss, while apparently being completely ignorant of the tragic events football has caused in other parts of the world.
